recipe.title: Wagyu Filet and Burrata Toast
recipe.time: 2 hr, or 30 min with the jam made ahead
recipe.headnote: Wagyu fat melts at a lower temperature than ordinary beef fat, so this filet wants a hard sear and very little time. Cook it like a normal filet and the marbling runs out into the coals and you have paid for nothing. Everything else on the toast is there to stand up to it: the burrata for cream, the jam for smoke and sharpness.
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb wagyu filet, centre cut, trimmed
1 large sourdough loaf, cut into 16 slices about 1/2 inch thick
2 lb ripe plum tomatoes, halved lengthways
method: For the jam, set the tomatoes cut side up on the cool side of Kettle A with a wood chunk on the coals. Lid on, vents half open, **45 minutes**, until they have slumped and taken on colour.

Chop them roughly and put them in a small pan with the shallot, sugar, vinegar, chilli and salt. Simmer over the cool side, stirring more often as it thickens, **40 to 45 minutes**, until a spoon dragged across the bottom leaves a clean line. Cool to room temperature.
Salt the filet an hour ahead and leave it on a rack at room temperature. Take the burrata out of the fridge at the same time; cold burrata tastes of nothing.

Sear the filet directly over the hottest part of Kettle A, turning a quarter turn every 90 seconds, until crusted on all sides. Move it to the cool side, lid on, until it reads **125°F** at the centre, about **10 to 15 minutes** in total.
Rest it **10 minutes** and pepper it now, not before, so the pepper does not scorch.
While it rests, brush the bread with oil and toast it over the hot side, about 1 minute a side, then rub each slice once with the cut garlic.
Slice the filet as thinly as you can across the grain. Spread each toast with jam, tear burrata over it, lay beef on top and finish with flaky salt and a torn basil leaf.

notes.label: Watch out
notes.text: The fat renders fast and flares hard. If the fire jumps, move the filet to the cool side for a moment rather than closing the lid on it, which smothers the flame but coats the meat in soot.

notes.label: Make ahead
notes.text: The jam keeps two weeks in the fridge and is better after a day. Bring it back to room temperature before spreading.

notes.label: On the beef
notes.text: This is written for American or Australian wagyu. Japanese A5 is too rich to eat in these quantities; if that is what you have, halve the amount and slice it thinner still.

plating.text: Assembled on the board at the last moment and passed by hand, one toast each, before anyone has sat down. The burrata goes limp if they wait.

menuLine.note: with smoked tomato jam, passed before anyone sits

items.note: Filet and toast share the hot side. Toast the bread while the beef rests, not alongside it.
Only on the day if the jam is not made ahead.

timelineAdds.what: Smoke the tomatoes on the cool side of Kettle A, then cook down the jam. Or make it up to two weeks ahead.
Salt the wagyu and leave it out. Burrata out of the fridge.
Sear the wagyu on Kettle A, then finish on the cool side to 125°F.
Toast the bread while the beef rests. Slice and assemble.
